good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “First 30-Day waiting Period… Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident”
good.explanation: Treatment for any illness is not covered for the first 30 days from the policy start date, but accidents are covered immediately. This is a standard waiting period and mainly affects claims made soon after buying the policy.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “Specific Waiting Period… excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage”
good.explanation: Certain listed diseases/procedures are not covered until you complete 24 months of continuous coverage. This is market-standard and delays coverage for those specific conditions.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Pre-existing Disease… shall be excluded until the expiry of 48 months of continuous coverage”
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered until the expiry of 48 months (4 years) of continuous coverage. This is common in retail health insurance and is important if you already have diagnosed conditions.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: “Automatic Recharge… re-instatement of up to the Sum Insured once in a policy year… The Recharge shall be available only for all future Claims which are not in relation to any Illness or Injury for which a Claim has already been admitted”
good.explanation: Up to 100% of the Sum Insured is reinstated once in a policy year after it is used, but only for future claims unrelated to the illness/injury already claimed. This helps if a second, different hospitalization happens in the same year.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “Relevant Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 30 days immediately prior”
good.explanation: Medical expenses for up to 30 days immediately before hospitalization are covered if related to the hospitalization. This reduces out-of-pocket costs for tests and consultations leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “Relevant Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 60 days immediately after”
good.explanation: Medical expenses for up to 60 days immediately after discharge are covered if related to the hospitalization. This helps pay for follow-up medicines and check-ups after you leave the hospital.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: “If the Policy Schedule states ‘Single Private Room’ as eligible Room Category… payable by the Company is limited to stay in a Single Private Room.”
bad.explanation: Room eligibility is limited to a Single Private Room when stated in the Policy Schedule. Choosing a higher category room can increase your share of the bill due to room-category linked deductions.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “Co-payment – 20% per claim, where age of insured / eldest member is 61 years or above”
bad.reference: Customer Information Sheet / KFD table (Clause 2(g) referenced)
bad.explanation: A 20% co-payment per claim applies when the insured/eldest member is 61 years or above. This means you pay 20% of every admissible claim amount, increasing out-of-pocket costs for seniors.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: “Expenses incurred on treatment for Named Ailments / Procedures… up to the amount specified against each… in the Policy Schedule… (These conditions will apply only if specifically mentioned in the Policy Schedule)”
bad.explanation: Named ailments/procedures can have payout caps up to the amount shown in the Policy Schedule, if mentioned there. This can leave you paying the balance if the hospital bill exceeds the sub-limit.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – II to Policy Terms & Conditions).”
bad.explanation: Items listed as non-medical in Annexure II are permanently excluded from cover. This typically increases your hospital out-of-pocket spend on consumables and similar items.

bad.name: NCB
bad.quote: “In the event of a Claim occurring during any Policy Year, the accrued No Claims Bonus will be reduced by 10% of the Sum Insured at the commencement of next Policy Year”
bad.explanation: After a claim, the accrued No Claims Bonus is reduced by 10% of the Sum Insured at the next policy year start. This means your accumulated bonus can shrink after claims instead of staying fully protected.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “A mandatory Co-Payment of 10% per Claim is applicable, which will be in addition to any other co-payment (if any) applicable in the Policy.”
bad.explanation: Global coverage claims have a mandatory 10% co-payment per claim, in addition to any other co-pay in the policy. This increases your share of costs when using the overseas benefit.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “If age of Insured Person or eldest Insured Person (in case of Floater) is 61 years or more, the Company provides an option… to choose for co-payment option of 20% per claim… and thereby get a discount of 20% in Premium” AND “Co-payment – 20% per claim, where age of insured / eldest member is 61 years or above”
bad.reference: General Conditions 2 / Clause 2(g)(I) AND KFD loss sharing table (Clause 2(g))
bad.explanation: One clause describes a 20% co-pay for age 61+ as an optional choice with a 20% premium discount, while another states 20% co-pay applies for age 61+ without clarifying it is optional. This creates a conflict, so you should verify from the Policy Schedule/KFD which co-pay actually applies.

unclear.name: Built-in SI Buffer
unclear.quote: “Additional Sum Insured for Accidental Hospitalization' shall be utilized only after the Sum Insured has been completely exhausted;”
unclear.reference: Optional Cover 11: Additional Sum Insured for Accidental Hospitalization (Clause 3.11)
unclear.explanation: An additional sum insured for accidental hospitalization is available only after the base Sum Insured is completely exhausted. Since it is under an optional cover and the amount/availability depends on what you opt for, the real benefit depends on your chosen add-on and schedule.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
